smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring completely eliminates the interface segregation smell. PydapDataStore no longer inherits from or implements any write-related methods. All six stub methods (encode, encode_variable, encode_attribute, set_dimension, set_attribute, prepare_variable) have been removed from the class by virtue of changing its parent from the fat interface to AbstractReadonlyDataStore. No residual smell artifacts remain.

cross_file_coordination.justification: Excellent cross-file coordination across all 7 affected files. The refactoring systematically updates: (1) exports in __init__.py to expose both abstract classes, (2) imports throughout (api.py, pydap_.py, store.py, conventions.py) to use AbstractReadonlyDataStore, (3) type hints in function signatures to reflect the new interface distinction, and (4) the core common.py definitions. No dangling references, stale imports, or inconsistencies remain.

structural_soundness.justification: The refactoring establishes a proper inheritance hierarchy that respects interface segregation. AbstractReadonlyDataStore defines the read interface, AbstractWritableDataStore extends it with write operations, and client classes inherit from the appropriate level. The separation of concerns is clean, responsibilities are well-defined, and the structure follows SOLID principles. The duplicate class definition (two AbstractWritableDataStore classes) appears to be a diff artifact from reorganization.

code_quality.justification: The changes demonstrate high code quality: clear naming (AbstractReadonlyDataStore vs AbstractWritableDataStore explicitly conveys intent), consistent application of the new types across all signatures, proper inheritance relationships, and comprehensive type hint updates. The refactoring is clean, maintainable, and improves code expressiveness without introducing complexity.

interface_decomposition.justification: Interfaces are decomposed along perfectly cohesive boundaries: read operations in AbstractReadonlyDataStore, write operations in AbstractWritableDataStore. Each interface has a single, clear responsibility. The boundary is natural and aligns with the fundamental read/write distinction in data stores.

split_quality.justification: The split is exactly right: all unnecessary stubs are removed from PydapDataStore by moving it to inherit from AbstractReadonlyDataStore only. The interfaces are neither too coarse (forcing unwanted dependencies) nor too fine (creating fragmentation). Write-capable stores can extend AbstractWritableDataStore to get both read and write operations naturally.

read-only_store_interface_purity.justification: PydapDataStore achieves perfect interface purity by inheriting from AbstractReadonlyDataStore instead of the fat interface. All six write-related stub methods (encode, encode_variable, encode_attribute, set_dimension, set_attribute, prepare_variable) are eliminated from the class. The class now only implements methods genuinely needed for read operations, with zero stub/pass-through implementations.

write_interface_architectural_separation.justification: The architecture fully restores the read/write boundary. AbstractReadonlyDataStore contains read operations and encode methods. AbstractWritableDataStore inherits from it and adds write-specific operations (set_dimension, set_attribute, prepare_variable). PydapDataStore inherits only from AbstractReadonlyDataStore, while writable stores can inherit from AbstractWritableDataStore. The separation is clean, complete, and type-enforceable.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring is exemplary, completely eliminating the interface segregation violation through proper interface decomposition. By introducing AbstractReadonlyDataStore and making PydapDataStore inherit from it instead of a fat interface, all six stub write methods are removed, and a clean architectural boundary between read-only and writable stores is established. The changes are coordinated perfectly across all seven files with consistent naming, proper type hints, and no residual artifacts.
